intro.caption: Side B — your first performance! Rule 1: repeat only Gerald's lines, word for word. Rule 2: when the tape stops, say the line and get their answer. Rule 3: don't tell Gerald the answer — just press play. He'll know. Seat your subject, phone flat between you, face up. Play when you're both ready!

ind1.caption: 「TO YOUR SUBJECT」 Eyes closed — we're jogging backwards through time! You're ten, maybe twelve, last class of the day, pencil in hand, doodling the same little doodle you always drew — five, ten seconds of pencil. NOT a smiley face, NO mountains, NO bicycles, no circles or triangles — a REAL thing anybody would recognize! See it. Hold it. Never say it. Press play when they nod!

ind2.caption: 「TO YOUR SUBJECT」 Blow the doodle up — real thing, real size, right there between you! Now think of it as a WORD (a smiley face would be SMILEY). LETTER LUNGES: walk its letters one at a time… and again, slower! 「TO YOU」 Ask: “Do you have it?” A nod is enough. Play when they nod!

preflight.caption: From here you say ONLY Gerald's words. Shake out the shoulders. Big smile. Psychic posture. Here! We! GO!

20.caption: First rep — say it like you own it: “I can feel a letter in your word. An A. There's an A… correct?” Get their answer, then play.

21.caption: HA — there's the A! Next rep: “I see a T as well… yes?” Go get it!

22.caption: Two for two, superstar! Softer now: “Is that… an R?” Go!

23.caption: THREE in a row! Last letter — barely trust it: “Now I'm not sure about this one… an S?” Go!

24.caption: Aaaand that's a no — Gerald felt it coming from 1987. Not the tape's fault, not the subject's fault… do the math. Shake it off! Say: “No… no, it's leaning — it's an S. There IS an S.” Like you've never been wrong in your life!

25m.caption: A no — Gerald knew before your finger did. Chest out; say it as a FACT: “This thing you drew — it is NOT a living thing.” Nod = yes. Argument = no. Either way, press play — he'll feel it.

25.caption: Agreed — not alive! You're on the board! Next station: “Hold out your hand. Imagine it there. Could you HOLD it in one hand?” Go!

26.caption: A no — Gerald felt it through the magnetic particles, and tape particles don't lie. New station: “Leave the letters. Let me touch the thing itself. Is it ALIVE?” Go!

27.caption: There's the S — the crowd goes MILD! Now we work the SENSES. Say: “Reach out in your mind. Can you TOUCH it?” Go!

28.caption: No again — Gerald knew YESTERDAY. Letters are not your event, and that's FINE. Pivot to RAW IMPRESSIONS: “Forget letters. Forget words. I'm getting something warmer. Is it ALIVE?” Go!

29.caption: Held it — Gerald felt the grip from in there! Now: “Squeeze it. Is it HARD?” Go!

30.caption: A no — called it in 1987! Too big for one hand; big thoughts burn more calories. Say: “It's bigger than both of us. Tell me — do you OWN one?” Go!

31.caption: It's ALIVE — feel that cardio! Say: “Stand next to it in your mind. Is it SMALLER than you?” Go!

32.caption: A no — shocker (to you). Gently: “It relates to life… it's part of a day.” Then: “Do you have one at HOME?” Go!

33.caption: Touchable — now reach FURTHER, deeper stretch! Say: “I'm touching it with you… wait. I sense… LIFE. Is it alive?” Go!

34.caption: ALIVE! The impressions love you — the letters were just jealous. Say: “Stand next to it. Is it BIGGER than you?” Go!

35.caption: A no — Gerald knew, the same way he knows you skipped Side A's breathing drills. Close now: “Reach for it. Can you TOUCH it?” Go!

36.caption: WET?! A personal best! Say: “Scales. A little bubble over its head.” Stick the landing: “You drew a FISH.” Turn the screen around!

37.caption: A no — felt in the flywheel. Say exactly: “It's not alive — but it is FULL of life. It's where the life lives.” Watch their face. Then: “Square walls. A triangle roof. Smoke from the chimney. You drew a HOUSE.” Turn the screen around!

38.caption: Can't touch it — nobody can, that's the POINT! Say: “Of course you can't touch it. It's ninety-three million miles away — you drew it in the corner of the page with little lines coming off it. You drew the SUN.” Turn the screen around!

39.caption: Bigger, alive, older than everybody here! Say: “Roots down. Branches up. The leaves were one big cloud, weren't they. You drew a TREE.” Turn the screen around!

40.caption: Smaller — Gerald felt petals! Say: “A stem. Petals in a ring. You pressed harder on the middle. You drew a FLOWER.” Turn the screen around!

41.caption: Touchable — and someone in this story is holding its cousin! Say: “Long. Thin. A point at one end. You drew the thing you were drawing WITH. You drew a PENCIL.” Turn it around!

42.caption: Untouchable — called from inside the cassette. Say: “You drew it as a crescent — a little banana in the sky — with stars around it. You drew the MOON.” Turn it around!

43.caption: HARD — and cold, felt right on the tape heads! Say: “A stem. A bowl. A toast at the end of a long week. You drew a GLASS.” Turn it around — cheers!

44.caption: Soft, full of air — knew it the second they squeezed! Say: “It wants to be thrown. It spends its whole life leaving. You drew a BALL.” Turn it around!

45.caption: They OWN one — Gerald has been in it, spiritually. Say: “Four wheels. Windows. Parked outside a childhood house. You drew a CAR.” Turn it around!

46.caption: Don't own one — NOBODY does, it belongs to the sky! Say: “You drew it with little windows down the side, didn't you. You drew a PLANE.” Turn it around!

47.caption: Smaller, warm, and ignoring us both! Say: “Whiskers. Pointed ears. It's ignoring you right now. You drew a CAT.” Turn it around!

48.caption: Not smaller — it's exactly your size, always was. Say: “A round head. Stick arms straight out. A self-portrait, age ten. You drew a STICKMAN — you drew YOU.” Turn it around!

rman.caption: They ARGUED — Gerald felt it coming since the warm-up! An argument means a PULSE. Say: “You drew a person. Round head, stick arms straight out. That's YOU, isn't it.” Turn it around!

49.caption: At home — you ATE off yours tonight! Say: “Four legs. A flat top. The whole family around it. You drew a TABLE.” Turn it around!

50.caption: Not at home — it lives on the WATER! Say: “A little hull. A sail. You always drew the waves as tiny W's, didn't you. You drew a BOAT.” Turn it around!

51.caption: No S — and for ONCE a no is exactly what Gerald wanted! Stand tall: “It's not letters anymore. I can FEEL this one. It's beating. You drew a HEART.” Turn it around — big finish!

52.caption: FOUR for FOUR — flawless routine! Cooldown pace: “You were ten years old, bored out of your mind… and you reached for the sky. You drew a STAR.” Turn it around, superstar.

finale.caption: COOLDOWN. Let them have their moment — don't explain anything, not that you could. Today you were adequate: Gerald's second-highest grade. Hydrate — minds are mostly water. Press ■ to rewind for your next subject.
